## 2.1  Analyzing the raw data

```{r extracting the table, echo=FALSE}

#| fig-width: 6
#| fig-height: 4

##  Extracting the table from the pdf: - tabulapdf package codes:
ingots2 <- suppressMessages(extract_tables(url, pages=3))

#lets store it in a table:

table1 <- suppressMessages(ingots2[[1]])

#when I first did this this you couldn't view Ni, Ag and Sb separately they all went under concentration
##  Cleaning the table: - DATA202 codes
table1 <- suppressMessages(table1 %>%
                             separate(
                               'Concentration in PPM',
                               into = c("Ni", "Ag", "Sb"),
                               sep = " "
                             ))

#this should now have all the columns separate :)

#making sure all the columns are named correctly:
suppressMessages(names(table1) <- c(
  "Sample", "Cu", "Zn", "Pb", "Fe",
  "Ni", "Ag", "Sb", "As", "Co", "Cd", "Sn",
  "Te", "Bi", "Mn", "Li", "Al", "V", "Cr",
  "Rb", "Sr", "Ba", "Cu_Zn"
))

#as R was having a hard time using the table above we created a Data Frame of the Concentrations:

Cu <- as.numeric(table1$Cu[-1])
Zn <- as.numeric(table1$Zn[-1])
Pb <- as.numeric(table1$Pb[-1])
Fe <- as.numeric(table1$Fe[-1])
Ni <- as.numeric(table1$Ni[-1])
Ag <- as.numeric(table1$Ag[-1])
Sb <- as.numeric(table1$Sb[-1])
As <- as.numeric(table1$As[-1])
Co <- as.numeric(table1$Co[-1])
Cd <- as.numeric(table1$Cd[-1])
Sn <- as.numeric(table1$Sn[-1])
Te <- as.numeric(table1$Te[-1])
Bi <- as.numeric(table1$Bi[-1])
Mn <- as.numeric(table1$Mn[-1])
Li <- as.numeric(table1$Li[-1])
Al <- as.numeric(table1$Al[-1])
V <- as.numeric(table1$V[-1])
Cr <- as.numeric(table1$Cr[-1])
Rb <- as.numeric(table1$Rb[-1])
Sr <- as.numeric(table1$Sr[-1])
Ba <- as.numeric(table1$Ba[-1])
Cu_Zn <- as.numeric(table1$Cu_Zn[-1])

Ingots_Frame <- data.frame (Sample = c("S1","S2","S3","S4","S5","S6","S7","S8","S9","S10","S11","S12","S13","S14","S15","S16","S17","S18","S19","S20","S21","S22","S23","S24","S25","S26","S27","S28","S29","S30","S31","S32","S33","S34","S35","S36","S37","S38"),Cu, Zn, Pb, Fe, Ni, Ag, Sb, As, Co, Cd, Sn, Te, Bi, Mn, Li, Al, V, Cr, Rb, Sr, Ba, Cu_Zn)

# Removing Cu/Zn from the table
Ingots_F_no <- Ingots_Frame[,1:22]

knitr::kable(
  Ingots_F_no, 
  caption = "Figure 1: Main component and trace element 
  concentrations obtained by ICP-OES & ICP-MS techniques", 
  format = "pipe") %>%
  kable_styling(font_size = 14, latex_options = "scale_down")

```

## 2.1  Analyzing the raw data
```{r 2.1b, echo=FALSE}
Element_order <- colnames(as.data.frame(Ingots_F_no[, -1]))

Ingots_sum <- Ingots_F_no[, -1] |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = everything(),
    names_to = "Element",
    values_to = "Concentration"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    Element = factor(Element, levels = Element_order)
  ) |>
  group_by(Element) |>
  summarise(
    Mean = mean(Concentration, na.rm = TRUE),
    SD = sd(Concentration, na.rm = TRUE),
    Min = min(Concentration, na.rm = TRUE),
    Q1 = quantile(Concentration, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE),
    Median = median(Concentration, na.rm = TRUE),
    Q3 = quantile(Concentration, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE),
    Max = max(Concentration, na.rm = TRUE),
    IQR = IQR(Concentration, na.rm = TRUE),
    Kurtosis = kurtosis(Concentration, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

knitr::kable(
  Ingots_sum, 
  digits = 2,
  caption = "Summary Statistics of Table 1", 
  format = "pipe") %>%
  kable_styling(font_size = 15, latex_options = "scale_down")
```
## 2.1  Analyzing the Raw data
```{r basic summary, echo=FALSE}
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 6

#Summary of the Data Frame:
#invisible(summary(Ingots_F_no))

#code to make the summary into a table
#skim(Ingots_F_no[,-1]) |>
  #select(-n_missing, -complete_rate)
  

#box plot of the initial data: (no transformations) using ggplot:
#start by turing the data into long format:
Ingots_long <- Ingots_F_no[, -1] |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = everything(),
    names_to = "Element",
    values_to = "Concentration")

#notchbox
  
ggplot( 
  Ingots_long,
   aes(
     x = Element,
     y = Concentration
     )
  ) +
  geom_boxplot(
    notch = TRUE,
    fill = "#648FFF",
    colour = "grey30",
    linewidth = 0.7,
    outlier.shape = 21,
    outlier.fill = "#FE6100",
    outlier.colour = "grey30",
    outlier.stroke = 0.8,
    outlier.size = 3
  ) +
  geom_jitter(
    colour = "#785EF0",
    alpha = 0.1,
    width = 0.12,
    size = 2
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Element Concentration Spread Between Samples",
    subtitle = "38 Orichalcum Ingots | Notched Boxplots | Highlighted Outliers",
    x = "Element",
    y = "Concentration (PPM)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(
      face = "bold",
      size = 22
    ),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(
      colour = "grey30",
      size = 14
    ),
    plot.title.position = "plot",
    axis.text.x = element_text(
      angle = 45,
      hjust = 1
    )
  )

```

## 2.1.1  Inconsistencies in Percentages
```{r echo = FALSE}
main_com <- Ingots_Frame[c(1:5)]

#adding the sum of the main components:
main_com$percentage_total <- rowSums(main_com[c(2:5)])

per_table <- sum_main <- main_com |>
  summarise(
    across(
      c(Cu, Zn, Pb, Fe, percentage_total),
      list(
        Mean = base::mean,
        SD = stats::sd,
        Median = stats::median,
        Min = base::min,
        Max = base::max
      ),
      .names = "{.col}_{.fn}"
    )
  ) |>
  pivot_longer(
    everything(),
    names_to = c("Element", ".value"),
    names_pattern = "(.+)_(Mean|SD|Median|Min|Max)"
  )

knitr::kable(
  sum_main,
  digits = 2,
  caption = "Summary statistics for main component elements.")  %>%
  kable_styling(font_size = 35)
```

## 2.4 Henze-Zirkler Test For Multivariate Normality 

:::{.center}
$$
\begin{aligned}
\mathcal{H}_0 :& 
\text{ The data follows a multivariate normal distribution},
\\
\mathcal{H}_1 :& 
\text{ The data does not follow a multivariate normal distribution}.
\end{aligned}
$$
:::


## 2.4 Henze-Zirkler Test For Multivariate Normality  
:::{.center}
```{r, echo = FALSE}

HZoriginal <- mvn(data = logIngots1, mvn_test = "hz")

hz_table <- HZoriginal$multivariate_normality

knitr::kable(
  hz_table,
  digits = 2,
  caption = "Henze-Zirkler Test For Multivariate Normality"
)
```
:::

## 2.5 Performing Mad Transformations
::::{.columns}

:::{.column width="50%"}
```{r transformations-mad, echo=FALSE}
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 6

#Calculate medians and MAD for each column:
median <- apply(logIngots1[,-1], 2, median)
mad <- apply(logIngots1[,-1], 2, mad)


#print(median/mad)
#mad


MAD_summary1 <- as.data.frame(logIngots1[1:11,]) |>
  pivot_longer(
    everything(),
    names_to = "Element",
    values_to = "Concentration"
      ) |>
  group_by(Element) |>
  summarise(
    Median = median(Concentration),
    MAD = mad(Concentration),
    Skewness = moments::skewness(Concentration),
    Kurtosis = moments::kurtosis(Concentration),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

knitr::kable(
  MAD_summary1[1:11,],
  caption = "Median Absolute Deviation Summary Table",
  digits = 2,
  format = "pipe")%>%
  kable_styling(font_size = 20)
```
:::

::::


```{r outliers, echo=FALSE}
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 6

#Compute the robust z-scores:
z <- scale(logIngots1[,-1], center = median, scale = mad)

#Flag observations where any variable exceeds the threshold
outliers <- apply(abs(z) > 2.5, 1, any)

#list(outliers)

z_scores <- as.data.frame(scale(logIngots1[, ]))

# View the rows flagged as outliers
invisible(summary(logIngots1[outliers,]))

Ingots_clean <- logIngots1[rowSums(abs(z_scores) > 2.5) == 0, ]

```

## 2.6  Henze-Zirkler Test for Multivariate Normality

:::{.center style="font-size: 1.3em;"}
HZ test on OG data:
```{R Henze Zirkler, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

#

HZoriginal <- mvn(data = Ingots_F_no, mvn_test = "hz")
cat("Henze_Zirkler Test Results:\n")
print(HZoriginal$multivariate_normality)
```
HZ test after all transformations:
```{r he, echo=FALSE}
#HZ clean data:
HZ <- mvn(data = Ingots_clean, mvn_test = "hz")

cat("Henze_Zirkler Test Results:\n")
print(HZ$multivariate_normality)
```
:::

```{r UMAP, echo=FALSE}
## Trying stuff - Note Gaia couldn't get this to work ALICE
ICN <- as.data.frame(Ingots_clean[,-1])

ICN[] <- lapply(ICN, as.numeric)

scaled <- scale(ICN)

sil_avg <- numeric(25)


k <- umap(scaled)
PamMan <- pam(scaled, k = 3, metric = "manhattan")

UMAP_plot <- data.frame(
  UMAP1 = k$layout[,1],
  UMAP2 = k$layout[,2],
  Cluster = factor(PamMan$cluster)
  )


```

## 3.3  Fuzzy Cluster Analysis
::::{.columns}

:::{.column width="50%"}
```{r fu1, echo=FALSE}
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 6

#k-medoids for Fuzzy

Fuzzy_k <- FKM.med(scaled, k = 3, m = 2)

#silhouettes

#Table of Fuzzy_K$U:
fuz1 <- suppressMessages(knitr::kable(Fuzzy_k$U[1:13,],
             caption = "Fuzzy K Silhouettes Clusterings",
             format = "pipe")%>%
  kable_styling(font_size = 20))

fuz1

Fuzzy_Sil <- SIL.F(scaled, Fuzzy_k$U)

Fuzzy_Clust <- apply(Fuzzy_k$U, 1, which.max)

d <- dist(scaled)

sil_each <- silhouette(Fuzzy_Clust, d)
```

## 3.3  Fuzzy Analysis

```{r fuzzy2, echo=FALSE}
sil_df <- data.frame(
  obs = 1:nrow(sil_each), 
  width = sil_each[, "sil_width"],
  cluster = factor(sil_each[, "cluster"])
  )

ggplot(sil_df,
       aes(x = reorder(obs, width),
           y = width,
           fill = cluster)) + 
  geom_col() +
  coord_flip() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = mean(sil_df$width),
             linetype = "dashed",
             colour = "red") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(
    "#648FFF", "#DC267F", "#FFB000")) +
  labs(title = "Silhouette Plot",
       x = "Observation",
       y = "Silhouette Width") +
  theme_minimal()
```
